data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject only when the subject's behavior is underdetermined by the test's own construction, and describes it when the test is a tautological restatement of the subject's existing behavior. The 3-of-26 distribution is a magnitude artifact: the one shown-to-fail-first mutation is the only case where the test and the subject are not tautologically related, because the test was written against a different behavior than the subject's current one, and the magnitude of the observed loss is proportional to the distance between the test's construction-time behavior and the subject's present behavior.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If a guard written with zero construction gap still rejects a mutation because the mutation changes a property not observed at writing time, the tautology criterion fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the shown-to-fail-first mutation was later found to preserve all observed properties of the pre-installation behavior, the construction-gap mechanism fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the same author wrote a guard with an explicit construction gap in an ordinarily-guarded module and saw high mutation loss, the mechanism would be supported.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The constraint-description distinction is a measure of tautological distance. If a test is written by inspecting the subject and asserting its observed properties, the test is a tautology: any mutation that preserves the observed properties passes, and the test constrains nothing. If a test is written against a different behavior and then the subject is changed to match, the test and subject are separated by a construction gap, and mutations that fail to close the gap are lost. The shown-to-fail-first installation is the only case where a construction gap existed; all other guards were written with zero gap, so they are tautological descriptions.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
